salesTax.localNote: Dealers collect the city and county taxes where the dealership is located; on a private (casual) sale the buyer pays state and local use tax to the county licensing official in the county where the buyer resides; only one city and one county tax is collected per vehicle.

salesTax.taxName: Gross receipts (sales) and use tax on motor vehicles, paid to DFA at registration
salesTax.rateNote: Vehicles priced under $4,000 are exempt from Arkansas state sales tax, and used vehicles from $4,000 to under $10,000 pay a reduced state rate under Ark. Code 26-52-324 (with no trade-in deduction in that bracket). The calculator applies the full 6.5% state rate, so it overstates the tax on cars under $10,000.
salesTax.localNote: Local (city and county) sales or use tax is determined by the location indicated at registration and title application, and applies only to the first $2,500 of the vehicle price (so at most $25 per 1 percent of local rate).
salesTax.evidence: State Sales and Use Tax - 07/01/2013 - 6.500%
salesTax.note: No tax if total consideration is under $4,000: Ark. Code 26-52-510 (FindLaw copy https://codes.findlaw.com/ar/title-26-taxation/ar-code-sect-26-52-510/): 'If the total consideration for the sale of the new or used motor vehicle, trailer, or semitrailer is less than four thousand dollars ($4,000), no tax is due.' Used vehicles priced at least $4,000 and under $10,000 are taxed under Ark. Code 26-52-324 at 'two and eight hundred seventy-five thousandths percent (2.875%)' which 'shall be in addition to: (1) Any gross receipts or gross proceeds tax levied in the Arkansas Constitution' (FindLaw copy); the DFA mydmv page that states the combined rate for that bracket could not be fetched (redirect loop), so the commonly cited 3.5 percent combined figure is not verified here. Local cap: Ark. Code 26-74-220 (FindLaw): county tax 'shall be levied and collected only on the first two thousand five hundred dollars ($2,500) of gross receipts, gross proceeds, or sales price on the sale of a Motor vehicle'. Local rate range not captured.

tradeIn.evidence: Sales or use tax will be due on the difference between the total gross receipts or gross proceeds for the motor vehicle and any credit resulting from the trade in of any used motor vehicle or trailer.
tradeIn.note: Statute: Ark. Code 26-52-510 pays tax 'on the net difference' between the price and the trade-in credit (FindLaw). Exception: for used vehicles in the $4,000 to $10,000 reduced-rate bracket, Ark. Code 26-52-324(c) says the sales price 'shall not be reduced by: (1) The value of a motor vehicle, trailer or semitrailer traded in as part payment'. A credit is also allowed when the old vehicle is sold privately within 60 days (https://www.dfa.arkansas.gov/office/taxes/other-taxes/tax-credits-special-refunds/sales-tax-credit-for-sale-of-a-used-vehicle/: 'Tax is due on the difference between the purchase price of the newly acquired vehicle and the amount received from the sale of the old vehicle.').

docFee.capNote: The Arkansas Motor Vehicle Commission sets the dealer service and handling fee by rule at not less than $0 and not more than $129; Rule 8 fixes the maximum at $129 and it must be charged uniformly to all retail customers.
docFee.evidence: The amount that an Arkansas dealer may charge for Dealer Service and Handling Fees, allowed by A.C.A. 23-112-317(d) is not to exceed $129.00.
docFee.note: Statute text (FindLaw copy https://codes.findlaw.com/ar/title-23-public-utilities-and-regulated-industries/ar-code-sect-23-112-317/): 'The service and handling fee shall be no less than zero dollars ($0.00) and no more than one hundred twenty-nine dollars ($129)'. realcartips lists the Arkansas cap as $129 with a $120 average.

C. 3002(c) schedule: 'Where the purchase price is less than $400, there shall be a uniform rate of $8.00; Where the purchase price is $400 or more, up to and including $500, the document fee shall be $13.75' then $5.25 per further $100 (5.25 percent). salesTax.taxName: Title Ad Valorem Tax (TAVT)
salesTax.localNote: TAVT is a single combined state and local rate collected once at titling; no separate city or county sales tax is added, and vehicles subject to TAVT are exempt from sales and use tax on the sale and from the annual ad valorem 'birthday tax'.

The tax base is fair market value rather than the price paid (see privateSale.valuationRule). privateSale.collectedAt: Collected by the DMV at the time of titling.
privateSale.valuationRule: Tax is on the sales price shown on the title or bill of sale, with a $75 minimum; for vehicles less than 5 years old an Affidavit for Procurement of Title (SUT-1A) is required when the price is not within $1,500 of the NADA trade-in value.
privateSale.evidence: when the sales price is not within a $1,500 variance of the current trade-in value as listed in the NADA Official Used Car Guide.
privateSale.note: For vehicles more than 5 years old with a missing or incorrect price a Vehicle Price Certification (SUT 1) or a handwritten bill of sale signed by seller and buyer is accepted.

salesTax.taxName: Retail sales tax (6.5%) plus the additional motor vehicle sales/use tax (0.5%)
salesTax.localNote: Local sales tax and Regional Transit Authority tax are added; retail sales tax is destination-based (location where the customer receives the vehicle) and use tax uses the location where the vehicle is first used in Washington. The DOR pages fetched did not state the local rate range.
salesTax.evidence: Through Dec. 31, 2025, the rate is .3%. Effective Jan. 1, 2026, the rate is .5%.
salesTax.note: stateRate 7.0 = 6.5 + 0.5. RCW 82.08.020(1) (https://app.leg.wa.gov/rcw/default.aspx?cite=82.08.020): 'a tax equal to six and five-tenths percent of the selling price on each retail sale in this state'; 82.08.020(3): additional 'five-tenths of one percent of the selling price on each retail sale of a motor vehicle in this state'. DOR sales-and-use-tax-rates page: 'Sales tax collection is based on the location where the customer receives the merchandise or service (destination-based sales tax).' The DOR auto dealers rate page returned HTTP 403.

tradeIn.evidence: For purposes of the retail sales tax measure, the selling price excludes 'trade-in property of like kind.'
tradeIn.note: The seller must take ownership of the trade-in and reduce the price at the time of sale; cash back for part of the trade-in value does not qualify.

docFee.capNote: Documentary service fee may not exceed $200 per vehicle sale or lease, must be disclosed in writing as negotiable before the agreement is signed, and must be separately designated from the selling price.
docFee.evidence: An amount not to exceed $200 per vehicle sale or lease may be charged by a dealer to recover administrative costs
docFee.note: Most recent amendment shown: 2022 c 182 s 211.

titleFee.evidence: $40 upon the execution of a retail sale or lease agreement...through December 31, 2036
titleFee.note: RCW 46.17.100 as effective October 1, 2026: $15 standard certificate of title application fee; $40 when the title results from a dealer retail sale or lease, through December 31, 2036. DOL fee page (https://dol.wa.gov/vehicles-and-boats/vehicles/vehicle-registration/calculate-vehicle-tab-fees): '$15' for title application plus '$6.50 for the title only' filing fee and '$18 for title transactions' service fee.

registration.note: RCW 46.17.350 vehicle license fee $30 for a passenger car plus RCW 46.17.365 motor vehicle weight fee of $35 (4,000 lb or less), $65 (6,000 lb) or $82.50 (8,000 lb) through December 31, 2028 (rising to $35, $75 and $90 from January 1, 2029); plus $6 filing fee and $11 service fee per the DOL page, and RTA or transportation benefit district fees where applicable.

privateSale.collectedAt: Use tax at the same rate as retail sales tax is paid to the Department of Licensing (vehicle licensing office) when the title is transferred and the vehicle is registered.
privateSale.valuationRule: Use tax is based on fair market value; the purchase price is accepted as the value if it is no more than 20% below fair market value or the fair market value is under $7,500 (WAC 458-20-17802), otherwise documentation of a lower value is required.
privateSale.evidence: The purchase price is accepted as the vehicle's value if the purchase price is no more than 20% below the fair market value, or the fair market value is less than $7,500 (WAC 458-20-17802).
privateSale.note: DOR fact sheet REV 32 2511 (11/2/21). DOR motor vehicle sales/use tax page: 'use tax applies at the time the vehicle is registered with the Department of Licensing.'

salesTax.taxName: Consumers sales tax on motor vehicle sales, collected by the DMV at titling (shown as '6% titling sales tax' on the DMV page; formerly the privilege tax)
salesTax.rateNote: West Virginia charges a flat $30 instead of 6% when the net purchase price is under $500.
salesTax.localNote: WV Code 11-15-3c(j): 'no municipal sales or use tax or local sales or use tax...shall be imposed...on sales of motor vehicles as defined in this article'.
salesTax.evidence: Standard fees include a $15.00 title fee, a 6% titling sales tax on vehicles with a net purchase price over $500 (or a flat $30.00 if the net price is under $500)
salesTax.note: flatCap holds the $30 flat tax for a net price under $500. Statute https://code.wvlegislature.gov/11-15-3c/: 'the rate of tax imposed by this section shall increase to six percent of the sales price for purchases of motor vehicles made on and after' July 1, 2017; 11-15-3c(g): 'the Division of Motor Vehicles shall collect the tax imposed by this section'. The older privilege tax in 17A-3-4 was abolished July 1, 2008 and replaced by 11-15-3c. Imposed under a vehicle-specific section but named the consumers sales tax, hence rateType sales.

tradeIn.evidence: so much of the sale price or consideration as is represented by the exchange of other vehicles on which the tax imposed by this section...has been paid by the purchaser shall be deducted from the total actual sale price paid for the motor vehicle
tradeIn.note: DMV page: 'If a vehicle trade-in is part of the deal, the 6% titling tax is calculated on the net purchase price (Purchase Price minus Trade-In Value).'

docFee.capNote: Cap set by the DMV Dealer Advisory Board: raised from $499 to $575 effective July 1, 2024; from July 1, 2025 the cap is tied to the BLS consumer price index and adjusted annually, so the figure in force in September 2026 may be higher than $575.
docFee.evidence: The DMV Dealer Advisory Board held a meeting on May 23, 2024, and voted unanimously to increase the documentary (doc) fee cap
docFee.note: West Virginia Automobile and Truck Dealers Association article; quotes previous cap '$499', new cap '$575', 'This increase will take effect July 1, 2024.' The WV DMV dealer pages could not be located (404) and the statutory or rule basis was not found on the pages fetched. Cars.com (2018) reported an older $175 cap, now superseded. CarEdge (2021) average $250, also stale.

titleFee.evidence: $15.00 title fee
titleFee.note: '$10.00 lien recording fee (if applicable)'. WV Code 17A-3-4 text still shows 'a charge of $10 for each original certificate of title'; the DMV page's $15 is used.

registration.note: Class A (cars and trucks up to 10,000 lbs) standard plate $51.50 new and renewal, including the $1.00 litter fee and $0.50 insurance enforcement fee; hybrids add $100 per year and electric or alternative fuel vehicles add $200 per year (DMV brochure revised 05/2024). WV Code 17A-10-3(a)(1) sets the base at $50 with a CPI adjustment permitted every five years.

privateSale.collectedAt: Paid to the DMV when the buyer applies for the certificate of title.
privateSale.valuationRule: A vehicle two years old or newer bought from a non-dealer is taxed on its NADA Clean Loan Book value regardless of price; an older vehicle bought for less than 50% of book value needs a notarized bill of sale signed by both parties or tax is assessed on the full NADA Clean Loan Book value.
privateSale.evidence: Any vehicle not purchased from a registered dealer that is two (2) years old or newer will be taxed directly on its current NADA Clean Loan Book value, regardless of the private transaction price.
privateSale.note: For purchases above 50% of book value: 'The 6% titling tax will be assessed directly on the declared purchase price.'

salesTax.taxName: Sales and use tax
salesTax.localNote: County tax (0.5% in 70 counties; 0.9% in Milwaukee County) and the 2% City of Milwaukee tax apply at the rate in effect where the vehicle will be customarily kept; some counties have no county tax. localMax 2.9 is the sum of the two Milwaukee rates stated by DOR, not a figure DOR publishes as a maximum.
salesTax.evidence: The Wisconsin sales tax is a 5% tax imposed on the sales price of retailers who sell, license, lease, or rent tangible personal property
salesTax.note: Same page: 'Seventy Wisconsin counties have adopted a 0.5% county tax.' 'Milwaukee County sales and use tax increases from 0.5% to 0.9%, effective January 1, 2024.' 'The 2% city of Milwaukee sales and use tax is effective January 1, 2024.' Fact Sheet 2113: 'The retailer must collect and remit the county and/or city taxes in effect for the location where the item will be customarily kept.'
